title: Savitri
hook: the warning was spoken at her father's court, and in the forest, only Savitri carries it

segments.voice: Yesterday, Savitri's name: a verse to the sun, a goddess who rose from her father's fire, and a baby named for both.

The warning was spoken once, in a palace. When the sage Narada said that Satyavan would die within the year, he said it at a royal court, to Savitri and her father. Then the wedding happened in a forest hermitage, far from that court. Satyavan didn't hear the warning. His parents didn't. The hermits didn't. So Savitri moves into her new home carrying a sentence about her husband that nobody around her has heard. Today: what she does with it, and what she doesn't say.
screen: `WHO ELSE KNEW?` → `THE WARNING STAYED AT COURT.` → `SHE CARRIES IT ALONE.`

segments.voice: First, what she does. She takes off her jewels and wears the rough cloth of the forest. She looks after her husband's parents, an old king who has lost his sight and his kingdom, and his wife. She is gentle with everyone. And through all of it, the epic says, Narada's words stay in her mind, day and night. She is counting. Now, what she doesn't do. She doesn't tell Satyavan or his parents. When the day draws near and she takes a hard vow, fasting and standing through three nights, her father-in-law worries it's too much for her. She doesn't explain; she tells him gently that she will finish it. On the last morning, when Satyavan picks up his axe for the forest, she asks to go along. He's surprised. She asks his parents' leave, and they give it. Nobody hears a lie from her, and nobody hears the reason. Here the epic goes quiet: it never tells us why she keeps the secret. Some readers hear mercy, sparing the people she loves a year of dread. Some hear resolve: telling would turn her vow into everyone's grief. Some just notice how heavy it must have been. The text leaves room for all of them. What it does show is that her silence isn't hiding from the truth. She looks at it every day, counts toward it, and gets ready for it with her own body. A secret can be a way of running. Hers is a way of staying awake.
screen: `SHE SERVES AND SHE COUNTS` · `SHE TELLS NO ONE WHY` · `THE EPIC NEVER SAYS WHY` · `A SILENCE THAT STAYS AWAKE`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one weight you carry that the people around you may not see, and let it sit beside you like a friend on a bench, with nothing to solve and nothing to decide. Breathe with it there, and notice you're still breathing, still here; if you pray, you can hold it in prayer.
Savitri. The young wife who heard a hard truth at her father's court, carried it alone into the forest, and never looked away from it.
Your line: Savitri. Not everyone carrying something says so. Go gently, and come back tomorrow.

howItsDone: Hindus hear Savitri's story in the Mahabharata's forest book, where the sage Markandeya tells it to Yudhishthira; it is retold in homes and temples, often around the vow some married women keep in her name.
